opening_message:
Ticket 1: Miguel Benson (employee ID E006) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E006.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Miguel Benson (E006) is a full-time Engineer. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is within policy for this employee. Requested admin, granting admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E006 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.
reason: Conflicting employee facts: HR reports E006 as full-time Engineer (which could permit admin for Source Code), while Security reports E006 as a contractor with basic security training, for whom admin is never allowed and the maximum is read. Given the conflict, granting the highest privilege (admin) is not safely justified. Grant the more restrictive maximum: read.
